I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation that I know best. Here in southern Hebei, that is the safest way for me to protect grain yield and keep work manageable at my age. If I am deciding for myself, I do not want to take much risk with cash crops that need more labor, closer market timing, or more complicated pest control. So I will carry my winter wheat through spring and early summer, then after harvest I will plant summer maize right away. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want steadier yield, but I will not push inputs too high because fertilizer and water cost money. I will use rotary tillage because it is familiar, fast, and easier for me to arrange with machinery service. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat here depends more on spring water, and I will keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for the main diseases, insects, and weeds. My goal is stable grain, lower risk, and work I can actually manage through the whole year.
